bugs.title: SD card fails under ESP-IDF (err=0x107) but works under Arduino
bugs.environment: nomad-sentinel ESP-IDF project; Arduino core 3.3.11 works
steps_to_reproduce: Mount SD_MMC with pins CLK=5, CMD=4, D0=6
bugs.actual_result: All card commands fail with err=0x107
bugs.root_cause: UNKNOWN. Not yet diagnosed. Candidates: clock configuration, pin drive strength, marginal card socket contact, or a difference in the IDF SDMMC driver initialisation sequence.
bugs.notes: GPIO46 is documented as NOT a usable card-detect line; it reads HIGH with a working card present. Do not gate SD.begin() on it. The Arduino path passing does not prove the socket is sound.

bugs.title: tracker MQTT CONNECT never confirmed; CIPSEND prompt and CONNACK unreadable by line parser
steps_to_reproduce: Observe that MQTT-CONNECT sent is never logged
Note that MARK-CONNECTED is printed unconditionally regardless of outcome
bugs.expected_result: MQTT CONNECT sent, CONNACK received, payload visible to a subscriber
bugs.actual_result: No MQTT-CONNECT sent line. Socket opens, then nothing.
bugs.root_cause: Two defects. (1) AT+CIPSEND emits a '>' prompt that is not reliably newline-terminated, so the line-based reader blocks until its deadline expires and gives up before the prompt is seen. (2) Broker CONNACK bytes (20 02 00 00) are not newline-terminated, so a line parser cannot consume them at all.
bugs.notes: The unconditional MARK-CONNECTED log is itself a reporting defect: it makes a failed connect look successful. Any status derived from it is unreliable.

bugs.title: tracker GNSS wait loop exits after seconds instead of the intended 15 minutes
steps_to_reproduce: Flash tracker.ino with no GNSS fix available
Observe TRACKER-DONE-NOFIX after a few seconds
The loop condition reads t < 900000UL && !haveFix, with t += 1000 per iteration
bugs.expected_result: Wait up to 15 minutes for a fix
bugs.actual_result: Loop exits after roughly 900 iterations, i.e. seconds of wall-clock time
bugs.root_cause: The loop counter is incremented by 1000 per iteration as a stand-in for milliseconds, but each iteration does not actually take one second. The counter is a fiction; it does not represent elapsed time.
bugs.notes: This bug produced a misleading NOFIX result that could be mistaken for a hardware or signal fault.

bugs.title: PRD FR-3.1 specifies a non-existent AT command
bugs.expected_result: Per the PRD, this should return GNSS information
bugs.actual_result: +CME ERROR. The command does not exist on the A7670E. AT+CGPSINFO is valid.
bugs.root_cause: The PRD was written without validation against the actual module command set.
bugs.fix: Correct the PRD to reference AT+CGPSINFO. Recorded in ADR-002.
bugs.notes: This error was made by a previous agent too, and the resulting +CME ERROR was misread as a hardware fault. An error from a non-existent command is indistinguishable from a real failure unless the command set is checked.

bugs.title: Misdiagnosis: a modem in PPP data mode was read as a dead, latched-off modem
bugs.description: The original BUG-005 claimed the A7670E latched off after ATD*99# and could not be restarted from software, based on modem_recover and pwr_polarity both reporting total AT silence. That conclusion was wrong. The module was not off: it was in PPP data mode, in which AT commands are discarded by design. Silence on the UART was therefore the expected state, not a fault. The recovery probe tested the wrong hypothesis, and the 2x2 GPIO21 x PWRKEY matrix was uninformative for the same reason.
bugs.root_cause: Diagnostic error, not a modem fault. The probes assumed that AT silence implied a powered-down module, and never established whether the module was still in data mode. Two independent confirmations: (1) adding a guarded +++ escape before any PWRKEY pulse restored AT immediately; (2) once PPP actually negotiated, the same module ran a stable session and never needed a power cycle.
bugs.impact: Cost significant time and produced a false S1 blocker plus a false 'GPIO21 polarity ruled out' conclusion that was committed in 6b4a7ca. It also implied a hardware power-cycle requirement that does not exist.
bugs.workaround: Send a guarded +++ escape (preceded and followed by silence) before concluding the modem is unresponsive. Then drain the response buffer and probe with AT. A real power-cycle recovery path is still worth having, but it is defence in depth, not the primary recovery mechanism.
bugs.preventative_action: Any AT-silence recovery path must first try +++ and must never send a blind PWRKEY pulse, which is not idempotent. Distinguish 'in data mode' from 'powered off' before concluding a module is dead.
bugs.status_note: RESOLVED. Superseded by BUG-006, which describes the real cause of the failed negotiation. The hardware power-cycle workaround recorded earlier turned out to be unnecessary.
bugs.evidence: Guarded +++ restore: '"+++" escape accepted - modem was in data mode', after which AT answered normally. Later runs dialled, negotiated and held PPP to phase RUNNING with no USB unplug at any point. Original (invalid) evidence retained for history: modem_recover 5 baud rates x 3 PWRKEY hold lengths plus 8s GPIO21 LOW, all silent; pwr_polarity all 4 GPIO21/PWRKEY combinations silent.

bugs.title: lwIP PPP could not negotiate with the A7670E: three independent defects
bugs.description:
lwIP reached PPP_PHASE_ESTABLISH and transmitted a well-formed LCP Configure-Request, but the module never replied, so the link never progressed and no IP was assigned. Three separate defects had to be fixed; each one alone produced the same symptom of total silence, which is what made this hard to diagnose.

1. The UART was handed to PPP too early. lwIP sent its Configure-Request microseconds after the module printed CONNECT, before the module was listening. The frame was swallowed, and the module then ignored the later retransmissions too. A hand-built Configure-Request with identical framing, FCS and options was answered at T+15s, while the byte-for-byte equivalent frame from lwIP at T+0ms was ignored, which isolated the fault to timing rather than content. Fixed with a 2000 ms settle delay after CONNECT.

2. pppos_input_tcpip() posted to an uninitialised tcpip mbox. This core normally has that mbox created by tcpip_init() from the WiFi library, and this sketch never starts WiFi, so the first inbound byte died on 'assert failed: tcpip_inpkt .../api/tcpip.c:257 (Invalid mbox)'. The assert is in the receive path only, which made the link look like it came up and then vanished. Fixed by calling tcpip_init(NULL, NULL).

3. Core state was mutated without the core lock. This core is built with CONFIG_LWIP_TCPIP_CORE_LOCKING=1, so pppos_create() (which calls netif_add() internally) and ppp_connect() must run with the lock held. Without it: 'assert failed: netif_add .../core/netif.c:297 (Required to lock TCPIP core functionality!)'. Fixed by wrapping the create/configure/connect sequence in LOCK_TCPIP_CORE()/UNLOCK_TCPIP_CORE().
bugs.root_cause: The Arduino ESP32 core's lwIP is configured for a hosted, WiFi-oriented model: the core is initialised by the network stack, and the core lock is mandatory. A bare-metal PPP client that skips WiFi has to take responsibility for both. The two asserts are the core telling us exactly this, and the early-dial race is a modem-side timing requirement that is not documented for ATD*99#.
bugs.impact: PPP-over-UART could not be brought up, which blocked TASK-020, REQ-004 NAT routing and the ADR-005 framework decision. The 2 ms gap between CONNECT and the first LCP frame is a reliability hazard for any future firmware, not just this experiment.
bugs.workaround: None needed. All three defects are fixed in firmware/baseline/ppp_client/ppp_client.ino.
bugs.preventative_action: Keep the post-CONNECT settle delay and the core-lock discipline in any firmware that drives this module. When triaging a silent serial link, test timing and receive-path initialisation before suspecting framing or the peer. Record the MRU observation: lwIP advertised MRU=0, but the module answered an MRU=0 request when sent by hand, so MRU was not the cause and ppp_recv_config() is not required here.
bugs.status_note: RESOLVED and verified on hardware. PPP reaches phase RUNNING and stays up; see TEST-020 and BUG-005.
bugs.evidence: Serial captures on /dev/cu.usbmodem58750034621, firmware/baseline/ppp_client. Before: 'RESULT PPP_NEGOTIATION FAIL (45 bytes out, 0 bytes in)'. After each fix in turn: 'assert failed: tcpip_inpkt ... (Invalid mbox)', then 'assert failed: netif_add ... (Required to lock TCPIP core functionality!)', then 'RESULT PPP_NEGOTIATION PASS (phase RUNNING, 217 bytes out, 235 bytes in)' with 'PPP-IP local=100.76.140.112 gateway=10.64.64.64 up=1 mtu=1500'. Cold-boot repeat: 'PPP-IP local=100.77.131.255 gateway=10.64.64.64', 230 bytes out / 273 bytes in.
